controls.label: Expected glow
controls.qualification: An estimate, not a measurement: black-body color at its published equilibrium temperature, 1,780.97 K.
controls.notes: Nobody has measured HAT-P-36 b's heat. This is the color of a black body at 1,780.97 K, the equilibrium temperature its paper computes from its star's light (Chakrabarty & Sengupta 2019, equilibrium temperature (NASA Exoplanet Archive planetary systems table)). On 120 hot Jupiters whose day side Spitzer measured, the measured temperature is within 20% of this kind of estimate for 83% (Deming et al. 2023). Its star lights the day side. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of Tuiren's planets in this map from above, to scale, with HAT-P-36 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

HAT-P-36 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (22, 49, 76) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 373693175, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 9-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
